description-proc.eng: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. This strengthens and supports the timely detection, assessment and response to drug-related risks. Within this policy context, systematic investigation of drug metabolism is a cornerstone of clinical and forensic toxicology. Overall, the objective of this contract is to reinforce collective capacity across the EU to interpret toxicological findings and, critically, to improve the detection, identification, and timely reporting of exposure to NPS and other illicit drugs. title-proc.eng: 26842 Biogas reactor

description-proc.eng: Søndre Follo Treatment Plant IKS intends to expand the current test facility with 1 Antec 105 m3 plug reactor, to a total of 4 plug reactors with the aim of phasing out the current rotten tanks, i.e. procure a further 3 reactors of 105 m3 for pasteurisation and removal of the treatment plant ́s sludge. The procurement is for 3 complete reactors with instrumentation, as well as a number of consultant hours. SFR will carry out all of the technical building works and all integration with SFR ́s existing installations. SFR has carried out a study for a new sludge treatment facility consisting of 4 plug reactors of 105 m3. The study shows that Antec's technology safeguards SFR's need for pasteurising and digesting the sewage sludge. The study shows that Antec's technology is the technology that covers the municipality ́s need for a future-oriented, reliable and environmentally efficient sludge system. The choice of Antec technology is justified by documented advantages connected to waiting times, energy consumption, climate and environmental footprint, area requirements and operational costs as well as not least two years experience in the operation of test reactor. SFR has particularly emphasised that the plant shall have high operational security and low technological risk, and that the system must be suitable for municipal sewage sludge under conditions comparable with Norwegian conditions, including cold and hot seasons. Based on the study, SFR's need assessment and overall assessment is that alternative sludge processes do not achieve the same advantages that have been experienced since December 2024. Although other technologies can, in principle, fulfil the requirements for sludge treatment, they are not assessed to cover SFR ́s total need in an equivalent way when the requirements for environmental performance, energy use, area, operational security, maturity and implementation risk are assessed together. SFR tested the Antec technology in 2018 with a pilot of 3 m3. The test lasted for 6 months with very good results. In 2023 ENOVA granted support for a full scale project with the integration of 1 plug reactor of 105 m3. The reactor was integrated and operated in December 2024 and has since been operated as normal by SFR ́s operational personnel. The technology has advantages that SFR would like to bring along further and has therefore promoted a case to SFR's board of directors and supervisory board to procure a further 3 reactors so that the total number is 4 SFR ́s intention to procure and integrate a further 3 plug reactors presuppose positive decisions from SFR's board and supervisory board. If the board and the supervisory board at SFR agree to the setting, the technical construction works can start in Q1 - 2027 with the aim of 4 plug reactors in operation in mid October - November 2027. SFR has examined the market for relevant plug flow systems equivalent to Antec ́s technology and that can be integrated with the existing control system and SFR ́s technical installations and optimised systems. Based on SFR's assessment, Antec Biogas is the only mature and relevant plug-flow system. Antec Biogass can also document full scale operation and relevant references under comparable conditions and with the same technical system as the current Antec Reactor. The plug-flow technology is owned and controlled by Antec Biogas. Antec Biogas holds the necessary intellectual property rights, including patent/process competence, that is necessary to realise the relevant Plug-flow system by SFR ́s sludge system. SFR's assessment is therefore that the services that shall now be procured, due to sole rights/intellectual property rights, can only be provided by Antec Biogas. There is, after SFR ́s assessment, not equivalent technology or alternatives that can cover SFR ́s needs in an equivalent way. The lack of competition is not due to SFR having formulated the artificially narrow need, but That SFR ́s justifiable and documented need for a mature Plug-Flow system with the stated characteristics and references can only be fulfilled through Antecs Biogas patented technology. The procurement will therefore be carried out without a prior published competition pursuant to the procurement regulations § 13-4 letter b. The direct procurement is limited to the services Antec Biogas is alone in providing, including the necessary license/rights basis, process basis and process assistance.

title-proc.eng: Upgrade works to the existing Cootehill Enterprise Centre, including thermal performance improvements and environmental upgrades to the external building envelope andfaçade systems.

description-proc.eng: Upgrade works to the existing Cootehill Enterprise Centre, comprising thermal performance improvements and environmental upgrades to the external building envelope and façade systems. The works are divided into five separate options, each of which shall be individually priced by the Contractor and included within the Form of Tender. The five option prices shall also be combined to provide an overall tender sum. The options comprise: Option 1 – Non-Insulated Façade Upgrade: Upgrade and refurbishment of the existing external façade without the provision of additional thermal insulation, including new building signage. Option 2 – Insulated Façade Upgrade: Upgrade of the existing external façade incorporating additional thermal insulation to improve the thermal performance of the building envelope, including new building signage. Option 3 – Window and Door Replacement: Removal and replacement of the existing external windows and doors with new thermally efficient units, complete with all associated making good, flashings, sealants and finishes. Option 4 – Photovoltaic Panels: Provision and installation of a new photovoltaic (PV) panel system, including all associated supports, electrical connections, controls and ancillary works. Option 5 – Internal Wall Insulation: Provision of internal wall insulation to the identified existing external wall constructions, including all associated linings, finishes, junction treatments and making good. Tenderers shall allow for all labour, materials, plant, access, temporary works, coordination and ancillary works necessary to provide a complete installation for each option.

title-proc.eng: Development services for minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) device

description-proc.eng: We are seeking quotes for the development and manufacturing of a multi-lumen stent intended for minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS). The device is designed to lower intraocular pressure (IOP), a key factor in the progression of glaucoma, with the ability to regulate pressure post insertion. The development scope, estimated to about 2 years of development, includes optimising the stent design using in sil billiard modelling, prototyping, and in vitro testing with ocular models and extracted pig eyes. Manufacturing will involve precision techniques such as microscale injection moulding and extrusion, ensuring the production of a batch that meets the standards for preclinical testing. Approximately 100 units are planned for manufacturing to support the initial in vitro testing and a preclinical efficacy study in pigs.
